newsitem.title: CANADA: Loewen Group acquires California funeral firm.
newsitem.headline: Loewen Group acquires California funeral firm.

text.p: Loewen Group Inc., the target of a hostile takeover bid by rival funeral home operator Service Corp. International, said Friday it agreed to acquire Rose Hills Co. Inc. of Los Angeles for $240 million.

Vancouver, British Columbia-based Loewen is teaming up with Blackstone Capital Partners II Merchant Banking Fund L.P. of New York, to acquire the cemetery and mortuary operations and assets of Rose Hills Co. and The Rose Hill Memorial Park Association.
Rose Hills Memorial Park is the largest cemetery in North America, and its mortuary serves more families annually than any other one in the United States.
Loewen, North America's second-largest funeral home company, said the Rose Hill deal was in the works before Service Corp. launched its unsolicited $43 a share bid, worth $2.8 billion, on Tuesday.
Houston-based Service Corp. is North America's biggest funeral home company and a fierce rival of Loewen.
Loewen founder and Chairman Ray Loewen said Rose Hill will immediately boost the company's earnings.

"This transaction ... is part of Loewen's long-term growth plan to acquire strategic operators consisting of larger urban properties as well as small, family-owned funeral homes and cemeteries," Loewen said in a statement.
The Rose Hill deal, coming a few months after Loewen acquired Prime Succession Inc., may play a role in getting a sweeter offer from Service Corp., analysts said.
Last June, Loewen and Blackstone joined forces to buy Prime Succession, the largest privately held funeral home operator in the United States, for $320 million.

"I'm hard-pressed to think from any standpoint that this is negative. It's good for Loewen on its own and it's good for Service if it wins the day," said David Brodie, an analyst with CIBC Wood Gundy.
Loewen gets an immediate earnings boost and can buy Blackstone's majority stake in Rose Hill in four years.
"They could say, 'These things are going to kick in with a good return four years down the road, so we've got extra future growth, so stick with us,'" Brodie said.
But Rose Hill also makes Loewen a more attractive target and may help prompt a sweeter offer. Analysts said Service Corp. was rumored to be a rival bidder for California company.
In a interview, Service Corp. President William Heiligbrodt downplayed the Rose Hill purchase, saying it's "no real victory" for Loewen shareholders.

"We don't see how that's a 'win' situation," Heiligbrodt said, adding that its offer makes sense for shareholders of both companies. He declined to say if Service Corp. would pursue a hostile takeover, but noted that "we usually try to finish the things we start."
When asked about a possible role for Loewen's top managment if a friendly deal were completed, he said "we'd certainly like to talk about that."

Loewen and Service Corp. have been bitter rivals in gobbling up small independent funeral home operators across North America. Loewen said its board will meet some time over the next few days to decide whether to fight to bid.
Blackstone officials said Friday that they had not been approached by Loewen to help mount a defense.
"We're nowhere near to talking about what our role would be, if any, if they decided to launch any kind of defense," Blackstone spokesman Howard Lipson said.
"Other than to say, 'Look guys, we think you're terrific. If your plans call for something that involves private equity, we hope you think of us,' and I know they would," Lipson said.
Under the terms of the deal, Loewen and Blackstone will form a new company to acquire the Rose Hills operations.
Loewen will integrate its 14 funeral homes and two combination funeral home/cemetery operations in California's Los Angeles and Orange counties into the new company.
Loewen operates 931 funeral homes and 271 cemeteries across the United States and Canada.
Blackstone and its affiliates will be the major shareholders and control the board of directors in the new venture. But Loewen will have the option to buy Blackstone's interest after four years.
The deal is expected to close by mid-December.
